study.title: Background Subtraction Angiography with Deep Learning Using Multi-frame Spatiotemporal Angiographic Input
study.venue: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine

imaging.modality_detail: Raw (native) cerebral catheter angiographic frames as input; DSA computed from motionless series used as target; 12-bit DICOM downsampled to 512 x 512
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebral neuroangiography (common/internal/external carotid, vertebral and other injections)
imaging.frames_per_sequence: Acquisitions 1-6 fps; series with fewer than 16 frames discarded; models use 16 contiguous frames (1 to 16 input frames tested)

data_released.detail: IRB has not allowed raw angiographic data to be made publicly available

task.task_description: Motion-resistant, maskless background subtraction of raw neuroangiographic sequences via image-to-image regression with 2D+t networks trained on synthetic affine motion-augmented data derived from motionless DSA series.
task.clinical_application: Reducing misregistration/motion artifacts in cerebral DSA to avoid repeat acquisitions; potential real-time use in the neuroangiography suite

temporal_evidence.quote: The architecture utilizes 3D convolutional blocks in the encoding and decoding pathways, with additional deep supervision layers

metrics.metric: Inference time per feed-forward pass (16-frame 3D U-Net)

other_limitations: Mild misregistration artifacts persist in the synthetic 'motionless' DSA ground truth
Global RMSE/SSIM metrics fail to capture spatially localized inference errors
Loss of spatial resolution and small-vessel discontinuities near moving dense bony structures
Feature-based motion pipeline not robust stand-alone and fails with feature-poor masks
Motion augmentation limited to affine (rigid, in-plane) transformations
future_work: Optimize the motion threshold hyperparameter as larger datasets become available
Formal evaluation of inference predictions by expert clinicians
Unsupervised or self-supervised approaches for subdomains with complex motion (e.g. cardiac angiography)
